title: Simple Game Character Class
instructions: Complete the `Character` class implementation using `__init__`, `attack` method, and the `__str__` method to make two characters fight and display their status.
steps: Define the `Character` class with `__init__(self, name, max_health)` to set up instance attributes: `name`, `max_health`, and `current_health` (starting at `max_health`).
Implement the `attack(self, target)` method. It should reduce the `target`'s `current_health` by 10 and print a descriptive message.
Implement the `__str__(self)` method to display the character's name and health status (e.g., 'Hero [HP: 100/100]').
Instantiate two characters: `hero` (name: 'Knight', health: 100) and `foe` (name: 'Goblin', health: 50).
Print the status of both characters using `print()`.

solution:
class Character:
    def __init__(self, name, max_health):
        self.name = name
        self.max_health = max_health
        self.current_health = max_health

    def attack(self, target):
        damage = 10
        target.current_health -= damage
        if target.current_health < 0:
            target.current_health = 0
        print(f"{self.name} attacks {target.name} for {damage} damage.")

    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.name} [HP: {self.current_health}/{self.max_health}]"


# Instantiate characters
hero = Character('Knight', 100)
foe = Character('Goblin', 50)

# Hero attacks foe
hero.attack(foe)

# Print status
print(hero)
print(foe)
hints: The `attack` method must access and modify the `current_health` attribute of the `target` object.
The `__str__` method must return a string, not print it.
